BiblicalUsage: Batsa means to cut off, to finish, to be greedy for gain. The proverb says the ways of everyone greedy of gain take away the life of its owners, he who is greedy of gain troubles his own house, Isaiah says the Lord will cut off the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria, and Habakkuk woes the man who covets an evil covetousness to his house.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word ties greed to cutting, because the greedy man cuts himself off from his own house and from God. He takes and he loses, and I hold that the covetousness Habakkuk woes is the same greed the proverb warns will cost a man his life.
